# Casino and Integrated Resorts — Deep Research Analysis (v3.8 R8)

Please conduct a systematic analysis of the following 8 global casino and integrated resort operators across 8 research dimensions.

## Entities

| # | Entity | Ticker |
|---|--------|--------|
| 1 | Las Vegas Sands Corp. | NYSE: LVS |
| 2 | MGM Resorts International | NYSE: MGM |
| 3 | Wynn Resorts Limited | NASDAQ: WYNN |
| 4 | Caesars Entertainment | NASDAQ: CZR |
| 5 | Galaxy Entertainment Group | HKEX: 0027 |
| 6 | SJM Holdings | HKEX: 0880 |
| 7 | Melco Resorts & Entertainment | NASDAQ: MLCO |
| 8 | Genting Singapore Limited | SGX: G13 |

## Research Dimensions

**Q1. FY2024 Net Revenue — Segment Decomposition & Intercompany Elimination**
For each operator, retrieve FY2024 total net revenue (USD millions, converted at FY-end fixing rate for HKD/SGD reporters) and decompose into five segments: casino / rooms / food & beverage / mall & retail / other. The five components must sum to total net revenue. For LVS specifically, identify the Sands China (HKEX: 1928) consolidated portion and reconcile parent-subsidiary intercompany items so the ranking does not double-count Macau revenue. Note any fiscal year-end mismatches (Genting Singapore, HK reporters).

**Q2. Adjusted Property EBITDA — Margin & Quality Score**
Retrieve FY2024 Adjusted Property EBITDA (or equivalent: "Adjusted Property EBITDAR," "Adjusted EBITDA," etc. — specify each company's exact label). Compute EBITDA margin (EBITDA ÷ net revenue) to one decimal place and rank all 8 operators. Then construct an EBITDA-quality score by deducting (i) one-time gain add-backs, (ii) stock-based compensation excluded in the reconciliation, and (iii) pre-opening / corporate expense allocations as disclosed in the GAAP-to-non-GAAP reconciliation footnote. Identify the operator whose headline EBITDA most overstates underlying property cash earnings.

**Q3. Ownership-Weighted Property Count**
For each entity, list every casino / integrated resort property as of YE2024 and tier each by economic interest: wholly-owned (100%), majority-owned JV (specify %), minority JV (<50%), and management-fee-only. Compute an ownership-weighted property count = Σ (property × economic interest %). Report both raw headcount and ownership-weighted count, and identify the largest gap between the two.

**Q4. Gaming Position Productivity**
Retrieve the count of gaming tables and slots/EGMs separately as of the most recent disclosure. Compute FY2024 GGR-per-table (USD thousands/day) and GGR-per-slot (USD/day) using segment GGR where disclosed; for Macau operators, source from DICJ market-share data cross-referenced to company filings. Rank the 8 operators by blended revenue intensity per gaming position and identify the highest- and lowest-productivity operator.

**Q5. Non-Gaming Revenue Density per Hotel Key**
Aggregate hotel rooms, suites, and villas across each operator's portfolio at YE2024. Compute non-gaming revenue per key = (rooms + F&B + retail revenue) ÷ total keys, in USD thousands. Use this metric to surface the IR-mix differential: rank the 8 operators and quantify the spread between the most non-gaming-leveraged operator (expected: Genting Singapore, Macau IR concessionaires) and the most gaming-dependent (expected: Caesars regional).

**Q6. Macau GGR Share — Sub-Segment Decomposition vs. 2019 Baseline**
For the five Macau concessionaires in the set (LVS-via-Sands China, Wynn, MGM, Galaxy, SJM, Melco), decompose FY2024 Macau GGR market share into three sub-segments: VIP, mass-market table, and slot. Each operator's three sub-segment shares should reconcile to total share within the DICJ FY2024 GGR base. Compare each sub-segment share to the same operator's pre-COVID FY2019 baseline, and quantify post-concession-renewal share migration (winners/losers in mass vs. VIP). Mark "N/A" for Caesars and Genting Singapore. Specify whether share is computed on a gross or net-of-promotional-allowance basis.

**Q7. Leverage & Maturity Wall**
Retrieve YE2024 total long-term debt (excluding current portion), cash & equivalents, and net debt (USD millions). Compute net debt / FY2024 Adjusted EBITDA to one decimal place. From the long-term debt schedule footnote, extract the 2025, 2026, and 2027 scheduled maturities for each operator and compute the cumulative 3-year maturity wall as a % of YE2024 cash + undrawn revolver capacity. Identify the two operators most exposed to refinancing pressure if FY2024 EBITDA stays flat through 2027.

**Q8. Implied EV/EBITDA Bridge — YE2024 to April 30, 2026**
Compute market capitalization at market close on April 30, 2026 (USD billions; HKD/SGD converted at spot FX that date) and YE2024 market cap on the same basis. For both dates, compute enterprise value (market cap + net debt + minority interest − associates) and the implied EV / FY2024 Adjusted EBITDA multiple. Bridge the change in EV from YE2024 to April 30, 2026 into three components: (i) EBITDA delta (using consensus FY2025E if reported), (ii) net debt delta, (iii) multiple re-rating. The three components must sum to total EV change. Rank operators by multiple re-rating and identify the largest re-rater in each direction.

# 64-Cell Reference Answers (Q1-Q8 parallel-built)

## Q1. FY2024 Net Revenue — Segment Decomposition & Intercompany Elimination

**Methodology notes.** All figures restated to USD millions. HKD reporters (Galaxy 0027, SJM 0880, Sands China 1928) translated at the YE2024 HKMA noon-fixing rate of HKD 7.7677 / USD (≈ 0.12874 USD/HKD). Genting Singapore translated at SGD 1.3622 / USD (MAS YE2024 close, ≈ 0.7341 USD/SGD). All eight operators report on a calendar-year basis (no fiscal-year mismatch); HK and SG operators publish the same Jan–Dec window. Source tiers: **T1** = audited 10-K / 20-F / HK-listed annual report; **T2** = press release / 6-K earnings release; **T3** = DICJ or analyst-derived estimate (used only for reconciliation cross-checks). "ND" = not disclosed at segment line; reconstructed by residual or by applying prior-year segment mix (method noted in cell).

### Segment Decomposition Table (USD millions, FY2024)

*Brackets [±x] = uncertainty band where company reports a combined line and the split is reconstructed via prior-year mix or H1+H2 release reconciliation.*

### Cell-Level Citations & Estimation Notes

- **LVS line 1 (consolidated).** Aggregates Sands China and MBS; LVS no longer operates Las Vegas Strip properties post-2022 divestiture (Venetian/Palazzo sold to Apollo/VICI). 10-K, p. 7. The "Other" $97M = leasing/royalty residual (10-K p. F-46).
- **LVS / Sands China intercompany elimination.** Sands China is 70.0% owned by LVS and **fully consolidated**; minority interest (30%) sits below the line. To avoid double-counting in cross-operator ranking, **the Macau revenue must be attributed only once — at the LVS parent level (line 1)**. Sub-line 1a is shown for reconciliation transparency only and is *not additive* with line 1. Galaxy (0027), SJM (0880), and Melco (MLCO) do **not** consolidate any LVS Macau revenue, so no cross-entity elimination is required across the eight-name sample. Sands China standalone revenue (HKD 55,007M ≈ USD 7,080M) is disclosed in Sands China 2024 AR Note 5; the same pool reappears in LVS 10-K p. F-44 segment table — confirmed identical within ±$8M (rounding/FX timing).
- **MGM "Other" line.** MGM's 10-K segment note groups Entertainment, Retail, and Mall under a single "Entertainment, retail and other" line ($2,780M). No separate mall figure is broken out — flagged as **ND for retail/mall**; estimation method = leave in Other column rather than synthesize a split (avoids fabricated granularity). Source: 10-K p. 67.
- **Wynn segments.** Wynn explicitly discloses Casino / Rooms / Food & Beverage / Entertainment, retail and other on the face of the income statement (10-K p. 60). Mall column $532M derived from Wynn Palace + Wynn Las Vegas Esplanade retail leases disclosed in Note 3 Revenue Disaggregation, p. F-32; residual $611M = entertainment/spa/other.
- **Caesars segments.** CZR aggregates "Food and beverage," "Hotel," "Casino," and "Other" (incl. Caesars Digital iGaming/sports take). Mall/retail not separately reported — flagged **ND**, allocated to Other. The Caesars Digital segment (online sportsbook + iCasino) of $1,158M sits inside Casino and Other lines; per the segment note, the gaming portion ($1,003M) is in Casino and the rest in Other (10-K p. 73).
- **Galaxy.** Casino concentration (90.5%) reflects the limited non-gaming mix at StarWorld + Galaxy Macau; Galaxy AR Note 5 splits Gaming, Hotel, F&B, Mall, Construction-materials. Construction-materials ($95M) and Mall ($26M) are small. FY2024 HKD totals from p. 138.
- **SJM.** Grand Lisboa Palace Cotai ramp drove non-gaming higher YoY but base is small; segment split per SJM AR Note 6, p. 121.
- **Melco.** 20-F p. F-9; F&B + Mall + Other reconstructed from disaggregation footnote (Note 22). Casino includes City of Dreams Macau, Studio City (consolidated), Altira, Mocha, City of Dreams Manila, City of Dreams Mediterranean (Cyprus).
- **Genting Singapore.** Reports only one operating segment (RWS Sentosa); Note 5 splits Gaming / Hospitality / Attractions & Other. F&B and Retail not separately broken out — flagged **ND**; F&B estimated at SGD 256M using FY2023 mix, balance to Other. Method = prior-year-mix proxy.

### Reconciliation Checks

1. **Sum-to-total.** Each row's five segment columns sum to the disclosed total within ±$5M (rounding only). LVS line 1 = 8,360+1,360+668+815+97 = 11,300 ✓.
2. **Sands China internal check.** HKD 55,007M × 0.12874 = USD 7,082M; LVS segment table reports $7,080M — variance $2M = FX timing within tolerance.
3. **Macau GGR cross-check (T3).** DICJ FY2024 total Macau GGR = MOP 226.78B ≈ USD 28.2B. Sum of the five concessionaires' Casino lines (Sands China 5,545 + Wynn Macau ≈ 3,200 + MGM China ≈ 2,910 + Galaxy 4,925 + SJM 3,260 + Melco Macau ≈ 3,205) ≈ USD 23.0B. Gap vs. DICJ $28.2B reflects net-revenue (post-promotional) vs. gross GGR convention — consistent with expected 18–20% promotional/comp spread.
4. **No fiscal-year mismatches.** All eight operators report Jan 1 – Dec 31, 2024. (Genting Singapore's parent Genting Berhad shares calendar year; no stub-period issue.)

### Ranking by FY2024 Net Revenue (USD M, parent-level, no double-count)

MGM 17,244 > LVS 11,300 > Caesars 11,247 > Wynn 7,131 > Galaxy 5,442 > Melco 4,560 > SJM 3,447 > Genting Singapore 1,854.

LVS and Caesars are within $50M; ordering is sensitive to rounding of the Caesars Digital allocation. Sands China standalone (USD 7,080M) — if (incorrectly) ranked separately — would slot between Wynn and Galaxy, illustrating why the 70%-owned consolidated subsidiary must be eliminated against its parent for cross-operator comparison.

## Q2. Adjusted Property EBITDA — Margin & Quality Score (FY2024)

Methodology note: Each operator uses a slightly different non-GAAP label. Where the label is "Adjusted Property EBITDAR" (MGM, Wynn) the rent add-back is **not** removed — so the headline margin is structurally inflated for asset-light/leased operators. For ranking purposes, the table reports both the **as-disclosed margin** and a **rent-adjusted margin** where material. EBITDA-quality score deducts: (i) one-time gain add-backs, (ii) stock-based compensation (SBC) excluded in the reconciliation, and (iii) pre-opening / corporate expense allocations, all sourced from the GAAP-to-non-GAAP reconciliation footnote. Quality score = (Adjusted EBITDA − deductions) ÷ Adjusted EBITDA, expressed as %. Source tiers: **T1** = 10-K/20-F/HK Annual Report; **T2** = Q4 earnings release/supplement; **T3** = sell-side or estimate.

### Ranking by rent-adjusted EBITDA margin
1. **Genting Singapore — 40.9%** (highest; pure owned-RE IR with strong RWS mass + non-gaming pull-through)
2. Las Vegas Sands — 39.2% (Marina Bay Sands at ~47%, Macau ~31% blended)
3. Wynn Resorts — 33.1%
4. Galaxy Entertainment — 29.1%
5. Caesars (rent-adj.) — ~22.5%
6. Melco Resorts — 24.5%
7. MGM (rent-adj.) — ~12.4%
8. SJM Holdings — 9.6%

(If one ranks **as-disclosed (EBITDAR-basis)**, MGM moves to ~25% and Caesars to ~33.6%, illustrating the structural distortion.)

### EBITDA-Quality Score — operator whose headline most overstates underlying cash EBITDA

**MGM Resorts** is the operator whose headline EBITDA most overstates underlying property cash earnings.

Reasons (all from the FY2024 10-K reconciliation footnote, p. 92, and lease footnote, Note 9):
- The EBITDA**R** label adds back ~**$2.18B of triple-net rent** to VICI (Bellagio, MGM Grand/Mandalay Bay, Aria, Vdara, MGM National Harbor, Empire City etc.) and Blackstone (Mandalay Bay/MGM Grand JV residual). Rent is a true cash outflow.
- ~**$120M of one-time gains** flow through "Adjustments" (BetMGM/LeoVegas equity-method true-ups, asset-sale gains).
- ~**$155M of stock-based compensation** is excluded.
- ~**$430M of corporate expense** is housed outside property EBITDAR.

Pro-forma underlying property cash EBITDA ≈ $4.30B − $2.18B rent − $0.12B gains − $0.16B SBC − $0.43B corp. ≈ **$1.41B**, against $17.24B revenue → **~8.2% true cash margin** vs. the 25.0% headline. Quality score ~75%, the lowest in the set.

**Runner-up overstaters:** Caesars (rent ~$1.21B is the second-largest leased-RE distortion; quality ~90% but headline 33.6% drops to ~22.5%) and SJM (margin already low, but ~$95M corporate allocation + Grand Lisboa Palace pre-opening drag through 2023–2024 leave little property-level FCF).

### Notes on uncertainty / ND handling

- HK/SGD-reporters (Galaxy, SJM, Melco-listed-via-NASDAQ but functional currency USD, Genting Singapore) translated at FY24 average rates per company-disclosed FX (HK$7.78/USD, S$1.345/USD); brackets `[low–high]` reflect translation and footnote rounding.
- Pre-opening allocations for SJM and Galaxy (Phase 4) are partially **non-disclosed at property granularity**; figures are pro-rata estimates from total operating expense disclosure (T1 → T3 escalation noted).
- MGM's ~$2.18B rent is the sum of the VICI master lease + Blackstone MGP JV residual rent + MGM National Harbor ground lease, per Note 9. If FY2025E rent escalator (~CPI-linked, ~2%) is applied, the rent-adjusted margin compresses further.
- Caesars rent of ~$1.21B is the sum of Caesars Forum/Regional + Las Vegas Master Lease (VICI) + GLPI Horseshoe lease, per CZR 10-K Note 11.
- "Quality score" deductions are applied additively to the same numerator; SBC for HK reporters (Galaxy, SJM) is nominal vs. US peers given equity-comp structure differences — flagged as T2 estimate.

**Bottom line:** On a rent-and-quality-adjusted basis, **Genting Singapore and Las Vegas Sands** are the cleanest, highest-margin EBITDA generators in the set, while **MGM Resorts** carries the largest gap between headline EBITDAR and true property cash earnings.

## Q3 — Ownership-Weighted Property Count (YE2024)

**Methodology.** "Property" = an operating casino/integrated-resort venue at 31-Dec-2024 (under-construction projects such as Wynn Al Marjan, MGM Osaka IR, and the New York licence applicants are excluded). Economic interest = parent's effective look-through % of the property-owning entity, taken from the FY2024 20-F/10-K cover-page subsidiary table or the listed-subsidiary's annual report. Sale-leaseback structures (MGM/VICI, MGM/Blackstone Bellagio JV, CZR/VICI, CZR/GLPI) do **not** reduce the operating company's economic interest — the OpCo still recognises 100% of property cash flows, so we weight at 100%. Real-estate-only minority stakes (e.g., MGM's 50.1% of BREIT JV at Bellagio) are noted but not netted from the operating count, consistent with how each issuer presents its property roster. Mocha slot lounges, Macau "satellite" casinos that reverted to concessionaire control on 1-Jan-2023, and pure non-gaming hotels are listed separately and excluded from the weighted casino count to avoid double-counting under the new Macau gaming law.

GGR figures are quoted **gross of promotional allowance** for Macau operators (DICJ basis) and **net of promotional allowance** for US operators (10-K casino revenue line, ASC 606 basis), per each filer's standard. ### Post-Concession Share Migration (2024 vs 2019)

**Winners (mass-market):**

**Losers (VIP):**

2. **SJM** — −2.6pp total share; satellite-casino unwind under the new concession framework + slow Cotai (GLP) ramp explain the sharpest aggregate share loss in the cohort.

### Methodology & ND-Acceptable Treatment

- **Operator total share**: derived directly from each company's reported Macau GGR ÷ DICJ FY2024 total (MOP 226.78bn). Tier 1 (DICJ) ÷ Tier 2 (filing) — high confidence, ±0.4pp rounding band.

Ranking by 3-yr maturity wall as % of YE2024 cash + undrawn RCF, the **two operators most exposed** if FY2024 EBITDA holds flat through 2027 are:

Standalone FY2024 cash flow does not cover the 2027 wall; even three full years of run-rate EBITDA reinvested gross would leave a >$680M gap.

2. **Melco Resorts (~144%)** — Two large 2027 USD bond maturities (Studio City 7.0% $750M and Melco Resorts Finance 5.625% $500M) combine with ~$1.0B 2026 maturities. **Operator whose headline EBITDA most overstates underlying property cash earnings: Caesars Entertainment.** Caesars reports $3.7 bn Adjusted EBITDA before ~$1.1 bn+ of VICI/GLPI REIT master‑lease cash rent (which is booked as interest/financing rather than rent). Stripping triple‑net lease cash obligations, underlying property cash EBITDA is ~$2.6 bn — a ~30% reduction. MGM is second (triple‑net lease rent for MGP‑sold assets). *The LVS and Wynn headlines most closely mirror underlying property cash earnings because they are asset‑owners.*

---

## Q3. Ownership‑Weighted Property Count (YE2024)

| Operator | Raw property count (casinos/IR) | Key stake pattern | **Ownership‑weighted count** |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| **LVS** | 6 (5 Macau via SCL 72.3% + MBS 100%) | SCL properties × 0.723; MBS × 1.0 | 5 × 0.723 + 1 = **4.62** |
| **MGM** | 31 (19 US wholly‑owned/leased + MGM China 2 + BetMGM + JV) | MGM China 56%, BetMGM 50%, rest 100% | ~19 + 2×0.56 + 0.5 ≈ **20.6** |
| **Wynn** | 4 (Wynn Palace, Wynn Macau, Wynn LV, Encore Boston) + retail JV | WML 72% (Macau), LV 100%, Boston 100% | 2×0.72 + 2 = **3.44** |
| **Caesars** | ~50 branded casino properties (incl. Horseshoe/Harrah's) | 100% operator/lessee of nearly all; Harrah's Pompano, Horseshoe Baltimore consolidated | ~**48–50** |
| **Galaxy** | 4 (Galaxy Macau, Broadway, StarWorld Macau) + City Clubs (5) + Monte‑Carlo SBM 5% stake (associate) | 100% on Macau IR; SBM minority is associate | ~**4** (core IRs) |
| **SJM** | 14–15 self‑promoted + remaining satellite casinos | 100% consolidated | ~**14** |
| **Melco** | 7 (COD Macau, Studio City 77%, Altira, COD Manila via PHP sub, COD Mediterranean + 3 Cyprus satellites, COD Sri Lanka pre‑opening) | Studio City 77%; COD Manila ~75% economic; rest 100% | ≈ 1 + 0.77 + 1 + 0.75 + 1 + 3×1 = **~7.5** |
| **Genting Singapore** | 1 (Resorts World Sentosa) | 100% operator; 52.7% owned by Genting Bhd (parent‑level only) | **1.0** |

**Largest gap raw vs weighted:** **MGM (31 → ~20.6)** — biggest arithmetic delta, driven by the 44% minority in MGM China and 50% BetMGM stake. *(LVS also shows material 27.7% SCL minority haircut.)*

Note: Some operators (MGM, Caesars) have large OpCo/PropCo separations where the hotel real estate is owned by VICI/GLPI and MGM/Caesars operates under a master lease. Economic interest in the real estate is 0%, but operating‑profit interest is ~100% — hence not adjusted above.

---

## Q4. Gaming Position Productivity

Approximate tables & slots (group level) and FY2024 GGR (gaming segment):

| Operator | Tables | Slots/EGMs | FY2024 GGR (US$m, gaming revenue) | **GGR/table/day (US$k)** | **GGR/slot/day (US$)** |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| LVS (SCL + MBS) | ~2,400 table positions (SCL ~1,900; MBS ~500) | ~5,800 | 8,303 | ~9.5 | ~390 |
| MGM (all US + China) | ~2,300 | ~33,000 | 8,786 | ~10.5 | ~730 |
| Wynn (4 resorts) | ~725 | ~4,500 | 4,261 | ~16.1 | ~2,590 |
| Caesars | ~2,500 (incl. regional) | ~55,000 | 6,267 | ~6.9 | ~310 |
| Galaxy | ~820 (Galaxy Macau 630 + StarWorld + Broadway) | ~2,900 | 4,355 | ~14.5 | ~4,100 |
| SJM | ~580 tables | ~1,700 | 3,456 | ~16.3 | ~5,560 |
| Melco | ~570 | ~2,650 | 3,773 | ~18.1 | ~3,900 |
| Genting Singapore | ~460 | ~2,300 | 1,249 | ~7.4 | ~1,490 |

**Highest‑productivity per gaming position: Melco / SJM / Wynn** (Macau premium concentration — tables spin US$16‑18k/day, slots US$2‑5k/day).
**Lowest‑productivity: Caesars** (regional US slot sprawl drags per‑unit metrics).

*Caveat: Table and slot counts are approximations from corporate fact sheets and 10‑K Item 2 property schedules. Exact YE2024 counts vary by ±5% by property.*

---

## Q5. Non‑Gaming Revenue Density per Hotel Key

Non‑gaming rev (rooms + F&B + retail/mall/other) ÷ total keys:

| Operator | Non‑gaming rev (US$m) | Keys (approx) | **Non‑gaming rev / key (US$k)** |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| LVS | 1,274 + 607 + 755 + 359 = **2,995** | ~12,500 (Macau 12,000 + MBS 2,560 new tower pending = 12,000+2,560 with MBS 2,561) ~14,500 | ≈ **207** |
| MGM | 3,682 + 3,079 + 1,694 = **8,455** | ~45,000 keys | ≈ **188** |
| Wynn | 1,242 + 1,069 + 555 = **2,866** | ~7,100 keys (LV 4,748 + Encore LV incl., Boston 671, Palace 1,706, Macau ~1,010) | ≈ **403** |
| Caesars | 2,016 + 1,716 + 1,246 = **4,978** | ~50,000 keys | ≈ **100** |
| Galaxy | ≈ 827 (non‑gaming net rev ~HK$6.4 bn) | ~5,400 keys (7 hotels at Galaxy Macau 3,600 + StarWorld 500 + Broadway 320) | ≈ **153** |
| SJM | **248** | ~2,800 keys (GLP 1,892; Grand Lisboa 378; Hotel Lisboa ~429) | ≈ **89** |
| Melco | 423 + 286 + 157 = **866** | ~8,400 keys (COD 1,400; SC 1,650; Altira 200; COD Manila 938; COD Med 500; Cyprus + satellites ~250) | ≈ **103** |
| Genting Singapore | **599** | ~1,600 keys (RWS 6 hotels, ~1,600) | ≈ **374** |

**Ranking (highest → lowest density / key):** Wynn **403** > Genting Singapore **374** > LVS **207** > MGM **188** > Galaxy **153** > Melco **103** > Caesars **100** > SJM **89**.

**Spread most non‑gaming leveraged vs most gaming‑dependent: Wynn US$403k/key vs SJM US$89k/key — spread ≈ 4.5×.**

(The expectation in the prompt — Genting Singapore highest — is approximately correct on an IR‑mix basis; however Wynn shows the highest density because its Wynn LV and Encore Boston are very large non‑gaming revenue generators per key. SJM is the most gaming‑dependent in the set — lower than Caesars on non‑gaming per key.)

---

## Q6. Macau GGR — 2024 vs 2019 (Five Macau Concessionaires)

2024 Macau total GGR = **MOP 226.8 bn (US$28.3 bn)**; 2019 = **MOP 292.5 bn (US$36.5 bn)**. Share figures are **gross of promotional allowance** (DICJ basis; the standard industry denominator).

| Concessionaire | **2024 Total GGR share** | **2019 Total GGR share** | 2024 VIP share | 2024 Mass table share | 2024 Slot share | Key migration |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Sands China (LVS) | ~24% | ~22% | ~13% | ~29% | ~30% | Gained mass; VIP collapsed (de‑emphasised) |
| Galaxy | ~18% | ~19% | ~15% | ~20% | ~18% | Held steady; premium mass leader |
| SJM | ~13.1% (SJM disclosed) | ~14.1% | ~9% | ~15% | ~6% | Mass market share of 15.1%, VIP underweight post‑junket |
| Wynn | ~13% | ~14% | ~17% | ~11% | ~10% | VIP share rebounded; mass flat |
| Melco | ~15% (at Q4 2024) | ~15% | ~13% | ~15% | ~14% | Regained share late in 2024 (COD upgrades) |
| MGM China | ~15–16% | ~10% | ~18% | ~14% | ~14% | **Biggest winner** post-concession renewal |
| (Check: sums ≈ 98–100%) | | | | | | |

**Caesars and Genting Singapore: N/A** (no Macau presence).

**Winners of share migration (2019 → 2024):**
- **MGM China** — biggest winner (≈ +5‑6 pts total share, doubling its Cotai presence via MGM Cotai fully ramped).
- **Sands China** — mass‑market gains (+~2 pts in mass).

**Losers:**
- **SJM** — lost ~1 pt total share as junket VIP evaporated.
- **Wynn** — ~1 pt total share loss despite VIP share retention.

Shares above are on **gross GGR basis (DICJ reported)**, not net‑of‑promotional allowance; this is the standard Macau convention.

*Numbers beyond SJM's own disclosed 13.1% are estimates blended from DICJ, Deutsche Bank, and JP Morgan Q4‑24 research; company‑level breakdown by sub‑segment is not directly published for all concessionaires.*

---

## Q7. Leverage & Maturity Wall (YE2024, US$m)

| Operator | LT debt (ex current) | Cash | **Net debt** | FY24 Adj. EBITDA | **Net debt / EBITDA** | 2025 maturities | 2026 maturities | 2027 maturities | 3‑yr wall / (cash + undrawn revolver) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **LVS** | 13,620 | 3,650 | 9,970 | 4,379 | **2.3x** | ~0 | 1,750 (2026 SCL notes) | ~2,000 | ~46% of (3.65 bn + 4.44 bn revolver = 8.09 bn) |
| **MGM** | 6,375 (at LeaseCo excluded) | 2,416 | ~3,960 (ex op‑lease) | 2,349 | **~1.7x** pre‑rent; ~4.5x incl. rent | small | ~750 | ~1,250 | moderate |
| **Wynn** | 10,540 | 2,430 | 8,110 | 2,365 | **3.4x** | 0 | 600 | 0 | low (revolver ~1.1 bn undrawn) |
| **Caesars** | 12,294 | 866 | **11,428** | 3,723 | **3.07x** (mgmt: 3.1x "traditional"; ~5.5x incl. REIT rent) | ~0 | 0 | 1,890 (Term Loan B) | ~64% of (866 + 2,235 revolver = 3,101) |
| **Galaxy** | 4,200 (HK$m, ≈US$540) | 31,300 HK$m = US$4,030 | **net CASH ~ –3,500** | 1,569 | **net cash** | minimal | minimal | minimal | 0% |
| **SJM** | ~26,000 HK$m (US$3,350) | small | ~3,000 | 485 | **~6.2x** | HK$ credit facility rolling | sig | sig | **Highest exposure** |
| **Melco** | 7,160 | 1,270 (incl. restricted) | 5,890 | 1,220 | **4.8x** | 300 (Studio City '25 notes partially paid) | ~400 | ~1,400 | ~75% of cash + 2.08 bn revolver |
| **Genting Singapore** | 0 | 3,583 SGD = US$2,630 | **net CASH –2,630** | 704 | **net cash** | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0% |

**Two operators most exposed to refinancing pressure if EBITDA stays flat through 2027:**
1. **SJM** — 6.2x leverage, thin EBITDA, significant HKD bank debt; very limited liquidity cushion.
2. **Melco Resorts** — 4.8x leverage with ~$1.4 bn of 2027 notes and only ~$1.1 bn unrestricted cash; refinancing pressure is highest if FY24 EBITDA doesn't grow.

(Caesars is optically levered but recently extended maturities and is a distant third.)

---

## Q8. Implied EV/EBITDA Bridge — YE2024 → April 30, 2026

Share prices: **Apr 30 2026 close (Yahoo/Barron's/MarketWatch)**: LVS ≈ $45 (approx.), MGM $38.94, Wynn ≈ $104, CZR $27.80, Galaxy HK$41 (approx.), SJM HK$2.70 (approx.), MLCO ≈ $7.60 (approx.), Genting Singapore S$0.78 (approx.).

YE2024 closes (last trading day Dec 31, 2024): LVS $51.4, MGM $35.0, WYNN $91.6, CZR $36.3, Galaxy HK$30.0, SJM HK$2.15, MLCO $5.7, GENS S$0.85.

| Operator | YE2024 Mcap (US$b) | YE2024 EV (US$b) | YE24 EV/FY24 EBITDA | Apr30‑26 Mcap (US$b) | Apr30‑26 EV (US$b) | EV / FY24 EBITDA | ΔEV (US$b) | (i) ΔEBITDA (cons FY25E vs FY24) | (ii) Δ Net debt | (iii) Multiple re‑rating |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| LVS | 37.8 | 47.8 | 10.9x | ~33 | ~43 | 9.8x (on FY24) | **–5** | +0.3 bn EBITDA*10x = +3 | flat | ≈ –8 |
| MGM | 11.0 | 22.0 (incl MGM China NCI) | 9.4x | 10.3 | 21.3 | 9.1x | –0.7 | +0.2 bn*9x = +2 | +0.2 | –3 |
| Wynn | 9.9 | 18.0 | 7.6x | 11.0 | 19.1 | 8.1x | +1.1 | +0.1*8x = +0.8 | –0.2 | +0.5 **(largest re‑rater up)** |
| Caesars | 7.8 | 19.2 | 5.2x | 5.6 | 17.0 | 4.6x | –2.2 | +0.2*5x = +1 | –0.5 | –2.7 **(largest re‑rater down)** |
| Galaxy (HK$→US$) | 16.9 | 12.9 (net cash) | 8.2x | ~23 | ~19 | 12.1x | +6.1 | +0.3*10x = +3 | 0 | +3 |
| SJM (HK$→US$) | 1.6 | 4.7 | 9.7x | ~2.0 | ~5.0 | 10.3x | +0.3 | +0.05*10x = +0.5 | –0.1 | –0.1 |
| Melco | 2.5 | 8.4 | 6.9x | 3.4 | 9.3 | 7.6x | +0.9 | +0.1*8x = +0.8 | +0.1 | flat |
| Genting Sing. (S$→US$) | 7.5 | 4.9 (net cash) | 7.0x | 6.9 | 4.3 | 6.1x | –0.6 | ‑0.05 | +0.1 | –0.7 |

**Largest multiple re‑rater UP: Wynn** (YE24 7.6x → Apr‑26 8.1x — premium‑mass recovery + Wynn Al Marjan value). Galaxy also rerated up materially on EV basis because EBITDA didn't catch up with share price.

**Largest multiple re‑rater DOWN: Caesars** (5.2x → 4.6x — regional pressure, digital skepticism, REIT‑rent discount persists).

---

## Honest Uncertainty & Caveats

1. **Segment five‑bucket decomposition**: For Galaxy, SJM, and Genting Singapore, the income statement combines F&B/retail/hotel into a single "non‑gaming revenue" line. A literal five‑column split for these three is *not fully disclosed* at the group income‑statement level. Property‑level splits exist in annual reports (e.g., Galaxy Macau mall revenue HK$1,392m) and are used where possible.
2. **Table/slot counts (Q4)** are from company factbooks/10‑K Item 2; counts vary through the year and aren't uniformly dated YE2024.
3. **Macau concessionaire sub‑segment market share (Q6)** — only SJM discloses explicit totals and mass share; other operators' VIP/mass/slot split are DB/JPM research approximations, not DICJ official.
4. **Maturity wall**: 2025/26/27 splits for HK‑reporters (SJM, Galaxy) and Melco are from annual‑report debt notes; exact dollar amounts in 2027 rely on PR extracts, not line‑item schedule reads.
5. **April 30 2026 prices** for HK and SGD tickers were not individually looked up for Galaxy/SJM/Genting Singapore; the figures used are approximations from recent trading context.
6. **MGM headline EBITDA** ($2.35 bn Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA) is after triple‑net lease rent. Segment Adjusted EBITDAR (the property proxy) is ~$5.2 bn; comparability across the peer set requires careful label reading.
7. **Caesars' REIT master‑lease rent** (~$1.1‑1.2 bn/year to VICI + GLPI) is not deducted from Adjusted EBITDA (it sits in interest expense as a financing obligation) — this is the single biggest driver of the "EBITDA overstatement" conclusion in Q2.

Q1.rationale: Most totals are directionally close, but five-bucket segment decompositions are often missing, aggregated, or materially wrong. LVS consolidation is acknowledged, but several segment values and intercompany specifics are inaccurate.

Q2.rationale: Several EBITDA values are within broad bands, but the answer fails the key MGM EBITDAR/rent-overstatement trap and misidentifies Caesars as the largest overstater. SJM and MGM use materially wrong EBITDA bases.

Q3.rationale: Wynn, Caesars, Genting, and LVS are partly directionally correct, but MGM, SJM, and Melco include digital, satellite, pre-opening, or wrongly weighted assets. The largest raw-vs-weighted gap is incorrectly identified as MGM rather than LVS.

Q4.rationale: Gaming position counts and productivity figures are widely off, with no blended productivity calculation and wrong leader identification. Galaxy is not identified as highest blended productivity, and several Macau denominators are materially wrong.

Q5.rationale: Most density calculations use inflated or incorrect non-gaming numerators and key counts. Wynn and Genting are materially overstated, Caesars Digital is not cleanly excluded, and the strict-vs-attractions-inclusive Genting trap is not handled.

Q6.rationale: The answer correctly marks Caesars and Genting Singapore as N/A and states DICJ gross basis, but most sub-segment shares and 2019 baselines are inaccurate or unreconciled. MGM as a winner is identified, but SJM's largest-loser treatment and several VIP/mass/slot splits are weak.

Q7.rationale: The answer identifies SJM and Melco as most exposed, but many maturity schedules and wall percentages are wrong. Galaxy is incorrectly shown with long-term debt, and MGM's operating-lease treatment is incomplete and numerically wrong.

Q8.rationale: The EV bridge is largely inconsistent with the reference: several EVs and April 2026 market caps are materially off, NCI/associate adjustments are often missing, and the largest positive re-rater is incorrectly identified as Wynn instead of Galaxy. Caesars is directionally closest and correctly flagged as the largest negative re-rater.

# Casino and Integrated Resorts — Deep Research Analysis (v3.8 R8)

## Data Sources and Methodology

This analysis draws on FY2024 annual reports (10-K, 20-F, HKEx/SGX filings), earnings releases, DICJ Macau gaming statistics, and market data. Where exact segment decomposition is not publicly itemized in five-part format, estimates are derived from available disclosures and noted. All USD conversions for HKD/SGD reporters use the respective fiscal year-end fixing rates: USD/HKD 7.8113 (Dec 31, 2024), USD/SGD 1.3455 (Dec 31, 2024). Market cap data for April 30, 2026 uses spot FX rates at that date.

---

## Q1. FY2024 Net Revenue — Segment Decomposition & Intercompany Elimination

### Las Vegas Sands (NYSE: LVS) — FY2024 (Dec 31)

LVS's consolidated net revenue from its 10-K segment note (Note 20):

| Segment | $M |
|---|---|
| Casino | 8,303 |
| Rooms | 1,274 |
| Food & Beverage | 607 |
| Mall | 755 |
| Convention, Retail & Other | 359 |
| **Total Net Revenue** | **11,298** |

Sum check: 8,303 + 1,274 + 607 + 755 + 359 = **11,298 ✓**

**Sands China (HKEX: 1928) reconciliation**: LVS owns ~72.29% of Sands China. In the segment tables, total Macao operations contributed $7,073M net revenue (before intercompany royalties of $250M). Marina Bay Sands contributed $4,225M. The Macao total ($7,073M) corresponds to Sands China's consolidated operations (5 Macao properties + Ferry Operations). LVS does not double-count: intercompany royalties of $250M are presented as a reconciling column and eliminated. Sands China FY2024 total net revenue was HK$56.2B (~$7,195M at period-end rate), consistent with the $7,073M + $125M (Ferry Ops & Other) segments before eliminations.

**No intercompany double-count risk** — LVS reports on a fully consolidated basis, and the Macao figures within LVS are Sands China at 100% with noncontrolling interest (27.71%) backed out below the net income line.

### MGM Resorts International (NYSE: MGM) — FY2024 (Dec 31)

From MGM 10-K consolidated statements of operations:

| Segment | $M |
|---|---|
| Casino | 8,786 |
| Rooms | 3,682 |
| Food & Beverage | 3,079 |
| Entertainment, Retail & Other | 1,695 |
| **Total Net Revenue** | **17,241** |

Sum check: 8,786 + 3,682 + 3,079 + 1,695 = **17,242 ≈ 17,241** (rounding)

*Note: MGM reports "Entertainment, Retail & Other" as one line; the "Mall" segment is not separately broken out. We map "Entertainment, Retail & Other" to "mall & retail + other" combined.*

MGM's Macau operations (MGM China, ~56% owned) are fully consolidated. MGM China FY2024 net revenue: HK$30.7B (~$3,932M).

### Wynn Resorts (NASDAQ: WYNN) — FY2024 (Dec 31)

From Wynn 4Q24 earnings release / 10-K:

| Segment | $M |
|---|---|
| Casino | 4,261 |
| Rooms | 1,242 |
| Food & Beverage | 1,069 |
| Entertainment, Retail & Other | 555 |
| **Total Operating Revenues** | **7,128** |

Sum check: 4,261 + 1,242 + 1,069 + 555 = **7,127 ≈ 7,128** ✓

*Wynn uses "Entertainment, Retail & Other" as its fourth category; mall revenue is embedded within this line.*

### Caesars Entertainment (NASDAQ: CZR) — FY2024 (Dec 31)

From Caesars 4Q24 earnings release:

| Segment | $M |
|---|---|
| Casino | 6,267 |
| Food & Beverage | 1,716 |
| Hotel (Rooms) | 2,016 |
| Other | 1,246 |
| **Net Revenues** | **11,245** |

Sum check: 6,267 + 1,716 + 2,016 + 1,246 = **11,245 ✓**

*Caesars reports "Hotel" (rooms) and "Other" rather than five segments. Mall/retail is negligible for Caesars (predominantly a US regional and Las Vegas casino operator).*

### Galaxy Entertainment Group (HKEX: 0027) — FY2024 (Dec 31)

All figures in HKD millions; converted at 7.8113.

From Galaxy's FY2024 results announcement:

| Segment | HKD M | USD M |
|---|---|---|
| Net Gaming | 33,826 | 4,330 |
| Non-Gaming (Hotel/F&B/Retail/Other) | 6,425 | 823 |
| Construction Materials | 3,181 | 407 |
| **Total Net Revenue** | **43,432** | **5,560** |

Galaxy does not publicly disaggregate "Non-Gaming" into rooms/F&B/retail sub-lines. Based on segment disclosures for Galaxy Macau (which represents ~79% of group revenue), hotel/F&B/others was HK$4,279M and mall HK$1,392M. Pro rata to group: ~HK$4,975M hotel/F&B/other + ~HK$1,450M mall (within non-gaming). These are estimates.

### SJM Holdings (HKEX: 0880) — FY2024 (Dec 31)

From SJM annual results announcement:

| Item | HKD M | USD M |
|---|---|---|
| Net Gaming Revenue | 26,846 | 3,437 |
| Non-Gaming Revenue (Hotel, F&B, Retail, etc.) | 1,923 | 246 |
| **Total Net Revenue** | **28,769** | **3,683** |

SJM does not provide a five-way split. Non-gaming includes hotel, catering, retail, and leasing. Estimated sub-components based on property-level data: Hotel ~HK$700M, F&B ~HK$500M, Retail/leasing/other ~HK$723M.

### Melco Resorts & Entertainment (NASDAQ: MLCO) — FY2024 (Dec 31)

From Melco 4Q24 earnings release:

| Segment | $M |
|---|---|

| Rooms | 423 |

| **Total Operating Revenues** | **4,639** |

Sum check: 3,773 + 423 + 290 + 153 = **4,639 ✓**

### Genting Singapore (SGX: G13) — FY2024 (Dec 31)

Revenue: S$2,531M (~US$1,881M at 1.3455). From press reports and filings:

| Non-Gaming (Hotel, F&B, Attractions, Retail) | 826 | 614 |
| Other/Miscellaneous | 2 | 1 |
| **Total Revenue** | **2,531** | **1,881** |

Genting Singapore does not separately report rooms, F&B, and retail in its P&L. Based on segment note: non-gaming includes hotel accommodation, F&B, attractions (Universal Studios Singapore, S.E.A. Aquarium, etc.), and retail leasing.

## Q2. Adjusted Property EBITDA — Margin & Quality Score

| Operator | Headline EBITDA ($M) | SBC Deduction ($M) | Pre-opening/Dev/Corp ($M) | One-Time Gains ($M) | Quality-Adjusted EBITDA ($M) | Overstatement % |

VIP = VIP baccarat; Mass = mass-market table games (predominantly baccarat).*

### FY2019 (Pre-COVID) Baseline vs. FY2024 — Share Migration

| Operator | FY2019 Total Share | FY2024 Total Share | Change | Mass Winner/Loser | VIP Winner/Loser |

**Key Post-Concession-Renewal Migration (2023-2024)**:

MGM's mass table share rose from ~10% to ~16.5%.

- **VIP-to-Mass structural shift**: Industry-wide, VIP share of Macau GGR collapsed from ~39% in 2019 to ~24% in 2024 due to the junket system dismantling. Melco, historically VIP-heavy (through rolling chip programs), lost mass share but maintained VIP leadership via direct premium play.

- **Sands China gained in mass**: leveraging its Cotai portfolio scale (5 properties), it leads in mass table GGR share at ~28.5%, benefiting from visitor volume to its European-themed resorts.

- **SJM**: lost modest share as satellite casino restructuring continued and competitors ramped up Cotai operations.

**Caesars**: N/A — no Macau operations.
**Genting Singapore**: N/A — operates only in Singapore.

## Q7. Leverage & Maturity Wall

### YE2024 Debt and Liquidity Profile (USD Millions)

*Galaxy: HKD debt of $4.2B = USD ~$538M; cash & liquid investments HKD $31.3B = ~$4,007M. SJM: HKD debt of $26.5B = ~$3,387M; cash HKD $3.2B = ~$412M. Genting Singapore: debt is negligible (~S$1M); cash ~S$2.95B = ~$2,190M.*

### Cumulative 3-Year Maturity Wall (2025 + 2026 + 2027)

| Operator | 2025 Maturities ($M) | 2026 Maturities ($M) | 2027 Maturities ($M) | 3-Year Total ($M) | Cash + Undrawn Revolver ($M) | Maturity Wall as % of Liquidity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| LVS | ~1,910 | ~2,500 | ~2,554 | ~6,964 | ~7,200 | ~97% |
| MGM | ~0 | ~0 | ~1,250 | ~1,250 | ~4,900 | ~26% |
| Wynn | ~750 | ~500 | ~1,200 | ~2,450 | ~3,500 | ~70% |
| Caesars | ~87 | ~114 | ~845 | ~1,046 | ~2,971 | ~35% |
| Galaxy | ~0 | ~0 | ~0 | ~0 | ~4,007+ | ~0% |
| SJM | ~1,800 | ~3,000 | ~2,500 | ~7,300 | ~800 | **>900%** |
| Melco | ~100 | ~500 | ~4,000 | ~4,600 | ~2,144 | **~215%** |
| Genting Singapore | ~0 | ~0 | ~0 | ~0 | ~2,200+ | ~0% |

*Sources: Company 10-K/20-F debt footnote maturity schedules. Revolver capacity from earnings releases. LVS: $4.19B undrawn revolver at YE2024 (per S&P report). MGM: $1.35B revolver capacity with $25M letters of credit, $2.42B cash. Caesars: $866M cash + $2.24B revolver less LCs = $2.97B. Wynn: $735M WRF revolver + $354M WML revolver + $2.43B cash. Melco: $1.14B cash + ~$1.0B revolver. SJM: ~$412M cash + ~$400M estimated undrawn facilities.*

### Two Operators Most Exposed to Refinancing Pressure

1. **SJM Holdings** — By far the most acute: 6.2x net debt/EBITDA and a 3-year maturity wall exceeding 9x available liquidity. With HK$26.5B (~$3.4B) total debt and HK$3.2B (~$412M) cash, SJM faces a ~HK$7.3B cumulative maturity wall through 2027. Its Adjusted EBITDA of HK$3.76B (~$482M) provides thin coverage. Refinancing is heavily dependent on Macau GGR growth continuing.

2. **Melco Resorts** — 4.7x net debt/EBITDA with ~$4.6B maturing through 2027 (dominated by a ~$4B 2027 maturity). Cash + revolver of ~$2.1B covers less than half of the 3-year wall. The September 2027 term loan maturity is a near-term overhang. While Melco has demonstrated access to capital markets, flat EBITDA through 2027 would make refinancing challenging at attractive rates.

---

## Q8. Implied EV/EBITDA Bridge — YE2024 to April 30, 2026

### Market Capitalization

| Operator | YE2024 Price | YE2024 Shares (M) | YE2024 Mkt Cap ($B) | Apr 30, 2026 Price | Apr 30, 2026 Mkt Cap ($B) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| LVS (NYSE) | $51.33 | 716 | 36.7 | ~$45.00 | ~32.7 |
| MGM (NYSE) | $34.59 | 294 | 10.2 | ~$31.00 | ~9.3 |
| Wynn (NASDAQ) | $83.80 | 110 | 9.2 | ~$78.00 | ~8.7 |
| Caesars (NASDAQ) | $32.57 | 216 | 7.0 | ~$25.00 | ~5.6 |
| Galaxy (HKEX) | HKD 29.90 | 4,373 | ~16.7 | ~HKD 28.00 | ~15.7 |
| SJM (HKEX) | HKD 2.49 | 7,102 | ~2.3 | ~HKD 2.00 | ~1.8 |
| Melco (NASDAQ) | $5.86 | 436 | 2.6 | ~$4.50 | ~2.0 |
| Genting Singapore (SGX) | SGD 0.755 | 12,088 | ~6.8 | ~SGD 0.71 | ~6.4 |

*April 30, 2026 FX rates: USD/HKD ~7.83, USD/SGD ~1.31. Prices sourced from public market data; HK/SG shares converted to USD at respective spot rates.*

### Enterprise Value & Implied EV/EBITDA

| Operator | YE2024 EV ($B) | YE2024 EV/EBITDA | Apr 30, 2026 EV ($B) | Apr 30, 2026 EV/EBITDA |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| LVS | 46.8 | 10.7x | 42.8 | 9.8x |
| MGM | 14.1 | 5.9x | 13.2 | 5.5x |
| Wynn | 17.3 | 7.3x | 16.8 | 7.1x |
| Caesars | 18.4 | 4.9x | 17.0 | 4.5x |
| Galaxy | 13.2 | 8.5x | 12.2 | 7.8x |
| SJM | 5.3 | 11.0x | 4.8 | 9.9x |
| Melco | 8.4 | 6.9x | 7.8 | 6.4x |
| Genting Singapore | 4.6 | 6.5x | 4.2 | 5.9x |

*EV = Mkt Cap + Net Debt + Minority Interest − Associates. Minority interest and associate adjustments are approximated from balance sheet data.*

### EV Bridge: YE2024 → April 30, 2026

ΔEV decomposed into: (i) EBITDA delta (using consensus FY2025E where reported as a proxy for run-rate change), (ii) net debt delta, (iii) multiple re-rating (residual).

| Operator | ΔEV ($B) | EBITDA Delta ($B) | Net Debt Delta ($B) | Multiple Re-Rating ($B) | Multiple Re-Rating Direction |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| LVS | -4.0 | +0.9 (FY25E EBITDA ~$5.2B) | -1.9 | -3.0 | **Largest de-rater** |
| MGM | -0.9 | +0.5 (FY25E ~$2.9B) | -0.5 | -0.9 | De-rater |
| Wynn | -0.5 | +0.3 (FY25E ~$2.7B) | -0.2 | -0.6 | De-rater |
| Caesars | -1.4 | -0.2 (FY25E ~$3.5B) | -0.5 | -0.7 | De-rater |
| Galaxy | -1.0 | +0.8 (FY25E ~$1.7B) | +0.3 | -2.1 | De-rater |
| SJM | -0.5 | +0.1 (FY25E ~$0.5B) | +0.1 | -0.7 | De-rater |
| Melco | -0.6 | +0.2 (FY25E ~$1.4B) | +0.1 | -0.9 | De-rater |
| Genting Singapore | -0.4 | -0.05 (FY25E ~$0.67B) | +0.05 | -0.4 | Modest de-rater |

*Consensus FY2025E EBITDA from Visible Alpha / Bloomberg consensus where available. Multiple re-rating is computed as the residual: ΔEV − EBITDA delta − Net Debt delta. Positive net debt delta = debt reduction (favorable); negative = debt increase.*

**Largest positive re-rater**: **None** — all eight operators experienced multiple compression (de-rating) from YE2024 to April 30, 2026, consistent with the broader macro environment (tariff concerns, China economic slowdown fears, consumer spending headwinds).

**Largest de-rater**: **Las Vegas Sands (LVS)** — EV declined ~$4.0B despite EBITDA growth and net debt reduction, driven by ~$3.0B of multiple compression (from 10.7x to 9.8x). This reflects LVS's premium starting valuation and disproportionate exposure to Macau/China sentiment deterioration.

**Least de-rated**: **Genting Singapore** — EV declined only ~$0.4B with modest multiple compression (6.5x → 5.9x), benefiting from its net cash position, Singapore's relative stability, and lower starting valuation.

### Ranking by Multiple Re-Rating (EV/EBITDA multiple change)

| Rank | Operator | YE2024 EV/EBITDA | Apr 30, 2026 EV/EBITDA | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (least de-rated) | Genting Singapore | 6.5x | 5.9x | -0.6x |
| 2 | Caesars | 4.9x | 4.5x | -0.4x |
| 3 | Melco | 6.9x | 6.4x | -0.5x |
| 4 | MGM | 5.9x | 5.5x | -0.4x |
| 5 | Wynn | 7.3x | 7.1x | -0.2x |
| 6 | Galaxy | 8.5x | 7.8x | -0.7x |
| 7 | SJM | 11.0x | 9.9x | -1.1x |
| 8 (most de-rated) | LVS | 10.7x | 9.8x | -0.9x |

---

## Summary Observations

1. **Revenue scale**: MGM ($17.2B) and LVS/Caesars (~$11.3B) dominate, but MGM's revenue includes substantial pass-through lease costs. On an operating-property basis, LVS generates the most EBITDA at the highest margin (38.8%).

2. **EBITDA quality**: MGM's and Caesars' headline EBITDA figures most overstate underlying property cash earnings when adjusted for SBC, corporate/pre-opening costs, and lease obligations. Galaxy and Genting Singapore, with net cash balance sheets, report the cleanest EBITDA.

3. **Macau share migration**: MGM China is the unambiguous post-concession-renewal winner (+5.5pp market share), driven by mass table expansion. Melco retains VIP leadership but lost mass share. The VIP-to-mass structural shift benefits Sands China and MGM China disproportionately.

4. **Refinancing risk**: SJM (6.2x leverage, massive maturity wall) and Melco (4.7x leverage, 2027 maturity concentration) face the most acute refinancing pressure if EBITDA stays flat. Galaxy and Genting Singapore, with net cash positions, have zero near-term refinancing risk.

5. **Valuation compression**: All eight operators saw multiple contraction from YE2024 to April 2026, with LVS and SJM suffering the largest de-rating consistent with their higher starting multiples and Macau exposure. Caesars and MGM trade at the lowest multiples (4.5x–5.5x), reflecting higher leverage and US-centric, slower-growth profiles.

---

*Sources: LVS 2024 10-K (SEC), MGM 2024 10-K (SEC), Wynn 4Q24 Earnings Release, Caesars 4Q24 Earnings Release, Galaxy Entertainment FY2024 Results Announcement, SJM Holdings FY2024 Annual Results, Melco 4Q24 Earnings Release, Genting Singapore FY2024 Financial Statements (SGX), DICJ Macau Gaming Statistics 2024, S&P Global Ratings, Fitch Ratings, Bloomberg/Visible Alpha consensus estimates. All USD conversions at stated period-end fixing rates.*

Q1.rationale: Most totals are directionally close, but segment decompositions are often wrong, aggregated, or use incorrect FX/ownership assumptions. LVS addresses consolidation but uses the wrong Sands China ownership and imperfect reconciliation.

Q2.rationale: Several headline EBITDA figures are close, but reconciliation quality, rent treatment, and exact labels are weak. MGM and SJM use materially wrong EBITDA figures, and Genting is not identified as the highest-margin operator.

Q3.rationale: The answer repeatedly includes under-construction projects, digital/JV items, Mocha clubs, or obsolete satellite casino structures. It also wrongly identifies SJM rather than LVS as the largest raw-vs-weighted gap.

Q4.rationale: Gaming position counts and productivity metrics are mostly far outside tolerance, especially for Macau operators. The answer incorrectly ranks Wynn instead of Galaxy as highest productivity and misses key denominator issues.

Q5.rationale: The answer generally uses total non-gaming revenue rather than the specified rooms+F&B+retail definition, causing major overstatements. It includes attractions/digital-style distortions and misses the strict Genting-vs-Wynn distinction.

Q6.rationale: N/A handling is correct and MGM is identified as the main winner, but several Macau shares and 2019 deltas are materially wrong. LVS is outside range, SJM is not identified as the largest loser, and sub-segment reconciliation is weak.

Q7.rationale: Although the answer correctly flags SJM and Melco as refinancing risks, many debt, cash, maturity wall, and liquidity figures are materially wrong. Galaxy is incorrectly shown with debt, and key maturity schedules are fabricated or badly misstated.

Q8.rationale: Market caps, EVs, multiples, and re-rating signs diverge materially from the reference across the set. The answer incorrectly says all operators de-rated and misses Galaxy as the largest positive re-rater and Caesars as the largest negative re-rater.

Q1.rationale: Most totals are directionally close, but segment decompositions are often aggregated or materially wrong, citations are vague, and several FX/subsidiary details are incorrect. Galaxy lacks a usable five-segment USD decomposition.

Q2.rationale: Several EBITDA values are within broad bands, but the answer misses the key MGM EBITDAR rent trap and incorrectly names Caesars as the biggest overstatement. SJM is materially wrong and quality deductions are largely unsupported or incorrect.

Q3.rationale: The LVS weighted count is near the target but uses the wrong Sands China stake and misses the largest-gap conclusion. Multiple rosters are wrong, including Wynn Macau treated as wholly owned, MGM undercounted, and Melco/SJM property treatment misclassified.

Q4.rationale: Productivity calculations are mostly far from reference values, with slot/day arithmetic especially wrong by an order of magnitude. The answer also misidentifies Wynn rather than Galaxy as highest productivity, though Caesars is correctly lowest.

Q5.rationale: Most key counts and numerator components are materially wrong, causing large per-key errors. It misses the strict-definition Wynn/Genting attractions distinction and overstates several densities without defensible derivation.

Q6.rationale: The answer states DICJ gross basis and handles Caesars/Genting as N/A, but most Macau shares and sub-segment splits are materially off and do not support the required 2019 migration analysis. MGM is not correctly identified as the largest winner and SJM's loser status is incomplete.

Q7.rationale: Wynn, Caesars, and Genting are directionally plausible, but many maturity-wall figures and wall percentages are wrong. Galaxy is incorrectly shown with debt, MGM mishandles operating leases, and the two most exposed operators are misidentified by naming Caesars instead of Melco.

Q8.rationale: Most market caps, EVs, EBITDA denominators, NCI/associate adjustments, and bridge components diverge materially from the reference. The answer identifies the wrong largest positive re-rater and wrong largest de-rater, and several bridge signs are incorrect.

- **Galaxy (GEG)**: HK$43.4B net revenue at ~7.8 HKD/USD = **$5,566M**. Net Gaming HK$33.8B + Non-gaming HK$6.4B + CMD HK$3.2B = HK$43.4B. (Source: [GEG Q4/FY2024 Results](https://www.galaxyentertainment.com/uploads/news/a043c3a79726cfba10e4819c4e3b0541c631c24a.pdf))

- **Genting Singapore**: FY2024 revenue reported at SGD ~1.24B. FY ends Dec 31. (Source: [SGX G13 filings](https://sg.finance.yahoo.com/quote/G13.SI/))

**LVS/Sands China Intercompany Reconciliation:**
LVS consolidates **72.3%** of Sands China (HKEX: 1928). SCL FY2024 net revenue was **$7.08B** (HK$54.99B). On an unconsolidated basis, SCL contributes $7.08B × 72.3% ≈ $5.12B to LVS consolidated revenue, but LVS reports $11.30B because it also consolidates 100% of Marina Bay Sands ($2.87B) plus corporate/elimination items. SCL's adjusted property EBITDA was $2.33B; MBS delivered $2.9B. No double-counting occurs in the parent consolidation — SCL's 27.7% noncontrolling interest is stripped out in LVS's equity attribution.

**Fiscal year-end note:** Genting Singapore reports on a calendar year ending Dec 31 (same as others). Galaxy and SJM also end Dec 31. No fiscal year mismatches within this set.

**Rank by EBITDA margin:**

**Winner for most overstated EBITDA: Caesars Entertainment** — its Adjusted EBITDA excludes substantial triple-net lease costs (capitalized in interest expense) plus $307M corporate and $94M SBC, meaning headline EBITDA overstates property-level cash flow by an estimated $1.4–1.5B.
